Founded in 1992, Lincoln is an international Human Resources consulting firm dedicated to supporting leaders and managers throughout their professional lifecycle. Over more than three decades, Lincoln has developed extensive expertise in identifying, assessing, developing and supporting leadership talent across a wide range of industries and international environments.
Lincoln’s approach is based on a deep understanding of business ecosystems, industry dynamics, organisational challenges and the human factors that drive sustainable performance. We believe that leadership effectiveness can only be assessed and developed through the combined understanding of strategic business requirements, organisational context and individual capabilities.
To address these challenges, Lincoln brings together complementary expertise across Executive Search, Executive Interim Management, Leadership Advisory and Career Transition services. Through specialised industry practices and dedicated expert communities, Lincoln supports organisations in critical talent decisions, advisory, leadership assessment, executive development, coaching and succession planning.
A key differentiator of Lincoln lies in its dual perspective: combining deep sector expertise with advanced assessment and leadership evaluation capabilities. This enables our consultants to understand not only the strategic and operational requirements of leadership positions, but also the behavioural, cognitive and interpersonal factors that contribute to leadership effectiveness and long-term success.
Our experience includes the conception of leadership frameworks, assessment and development of senior managers, executives and leadership teams operating in highly demanding, international and complex environments. We regularly support organisations facing transformation, technological change, organisational complexity and increasing uncertainty, where leadership quality becomes a critical success factor.
Lincoln operates in a highly competitive market where excellence in talent identification and evaluation is essential. This environment continuously challenges us to refine our methodologies and maintain the highest standards of professional practice.
Convinced that uncertainty, complexity and continuous change are not only challenges but also drivers of innovation and development, Lincoln has invested in collaborative innovation initiatives aimed at advancing the understanding of leadership success. This commitment has led us to combine evidence-based psychological assessment, leadership research, behavioural observation methodologies and practical organisational experience in order to provide robust, fair and decision-relevant assessments.

DAPCOM Data Services is a software engineering company participated by the University of Barcelona (UB) and the Technical University of Catalonia (UPC). It produces professional software solutions mainly focused on scientific data, data processing pipelines, high-performance computing and efficient data compression strategies, including our own implementations and protected software as well as open source software (FOSS).
The company commercializes FAPEC, a patented data compression algorithm originally created for space communications but later extended with several algorithms including tailored designs. FAPEC offers an optimum compromise between CPU resource consumption and compression ratio, offering good performance even with noise and outliers present in the data to be compressed. FAPEC can have multiple applications in processing, transfer and storage of large data sets, such as in scientific research, supercomputers or in companies dealing with Big Data scenarios. Since 2023, it is being used in the maritime sector. DAPCOM also commercializes FARSHY, an advanced image viewer supporting raw hyperspectral imagery and watercolumn files.
DAPCOM was one of the first companies in Spain selected to take part in the European Space Agency Business Incubation Centre Programme in Barcelona (ESA BIC). The aim of this programme is the technology transfer from space developed technologies to terrestrial applications.

(Baden-Württemberg, Germany) developing an autonomous spray-drone system for steep-slope viticulture

firmware, onboard computing, custom electronics and mission software for computer vision, autonomous
mission planning and precise application control. Navigation is based on multi-GNSS positioning
including the European Galileo system, with a development path toward Galileo/EGNOS high-accuracy

terrain. SaidGor holds an operating authorisation from the German Federal Aviation Office
(Luftfahrt-Bundesamt) and is listed by the Julius Kühn-Institut (JKI) for spray equipment suitable
for steep-slope viticulture. The system aims to reduce plant-protection-product use and spray drift
and to remove operators from hazardous slopes. The company is currently in a pre-commercial phase and
is preparing its first documented field spray demonstration.

Kurs Orbital expands human activities beyond Earth by providing rendezvous and docking technology to start-ups and companies which would like to offer in-orbit servicing or logistics missions, but cannot afford the development time and cost for this technology.
ARCap is a standardised module, which enables any kind of spacecraft to perform such missions in a totally autonomous way, dealing also with non-cooperative targets like space debris, malfunctioning or out-of-fuel spacecrafts.
The algorithms running the ARCap module come from the soviet Kurs rendezvous-acquisition system, used continuously since 1985 and responsible for more than 300 successful dockings in orbit between Soyuz-Progress vehicles, the MIR and the International Space Station.

The Municipality of South Nicosia–Idalion has been established through the 2024 local government reform. The Municipality covers an area of approximately 100 km² and serves a population of around 25,000 inhabitants. The municipality includes the communities of Idalion, Lympia, Pera Chorio, Nisou, Alambra and Potamia, representing a diverse landscape that combines urban, semi-urban and rural environments.
The area hosts one of Cyprus’ largest agricultural production zones, with significant activities in dairy farming and olive cultivation, while also including one of the largest industrial areas on the island, creating a complex interaction between agricultural, industrial and residential systems. This mixed territorial profile generates increasing demands for climate resilience, smart resource management, sustainable land use, sustainable mobility and resilient infrastructure development.
The Municipality also holds strong cultural significance, as Idalion was one of the most important ancient kingdoms of Cyprus, contributing to a landscape where cultural heritage coexists with modern development needs. Due to increasing pressures from climate change, including water scarcity, heat stress and environmental degradation, the area presents a relevant case for testing integrated approaches that support the development of a more inclusive, sustainable and climate-resilient urban and rural environment.

TerraTeQ's technology integrates advanced sensing methodologies, edge processing, and Blues Wireless connectivity to support remote monitoring and data-driven decision making. Hochschule Geisenheim University was founded in 2013 as the result of a merger between the Geisenheim Research Institute and the Geisenheim faculty of the Hochschule RheinMain. Our university combines comprehensive research with application-oriented, practical teaching across a unique range of subjects, from wine and beverages to food, horticulture, and landscape architecture. The overarching topics of climate protection and sustainability are also an integral part of all of our degree programs and are at the center of our research.
Our Approach
We are Germany’s first Hochschule neuen Typs – a ‘new type’ of university – and are proud to have over 150 years of history behind us. Our origins date back to October 1872, with the founding of the Royal Prussian College for Fruit Growing and Viticulture in Geisenheim.
At the center of our approach is the holistic consideration of the entire value chain of specialty crops, including grapevines, fruits, vegetables, and ornamental plants. We are committed to studying the diverse production and processing methods of these crops, as well as food safety, food logistics, and the economics and marketing of wine and other beverages. Other focus areas at the university include cultural landscape development, urban open space design, landscape architecture, and conservation.

Our Mission
Research, education, praxis: this triad is at the beating heart of Hochschule Geisenheim University. Our goal is to find new and unique ways to make use of the interplay between these three areas; we conduct both applied and basic research, go far beyond fundamental teaching approaches with a range of practice-oriented study programs, and promote the transfer of knowledge into real-world application.
We currently offer a total of 7 practice-oriented bachelor’s degree programs, 5 of which are available as integrated work-study programs and all of which lead to a professional qualification. Additionally, we offer 10research-based master’s degree programs and also have the right to award doctoral certificates.
With around 50 professors (incl. apl, honorary and co-vocation professors) and numerous scientific staff members, our students are provided with extensive support and an excellent learning environment. Our students and researchers also benefit from our global network of renowned partner universities, institutions, and companies. Our degree programs, including two programs that are taught entirely in English, bring together students from over 50 different nations; approximately 14% of our current 1,400 students are from countries outside of Germany.
With more than 550 employees, Hochschule Geisenheim University is also a major regional employer. Our campus is nestled in the unique cultural landscape of the Rheingau region and has excellent connections to the broader Rhine-Main metropolitan area.

entityDescription:
Recycllux has built the end-to-end platform that connects satellite-based marine litter detection with coordinated field intervention and blockchain-secured impact verification. Earth Observation is the foundation of the system: the platform ingests Sentinel-1 (SAR) and Sentinel-2 (optical) imagery via Google Earth Engine, applies proprietary AI models trained on multi-temporal radar and optical data fusion, and identifies floating marine litter hotspots in coastal accumulation zones. Detection operates continuously, regardless of weather, cloud cover, or water turbidity, and achieves over 80% accuracy against in-situ ground-truth data, with ongoing optimisation targeting 85% and above. A patent on the core data-fusion method is being filed in H1 2026. 

The satellite intelligence is operationalised through a digital Intervention Portal that dispatches the nearest registered local actors, fishing communities and coastal NGOs, to recover and sort waste at the identified coordinates. Every kilogram collected is recorded and secured on blockchain, generating audit-ready reporting for MARPOL, CSRD, and EPR compliance. The model is asset-light: no proprietary vessels, no offshore hardware, and a carbon footprint approximately 46 times lower than conventional industrial cleanup approaches. 

The platform is commercially validated. In September 2025, Recycllux completed its first paid intervention on the Romanian Black Sea coast, coordinating 15 fishers and two environmental NGOs to recover 87 kg of marine waste with 88.24% recycling rate and 131.82 kg CO₂ avoided. Two paying customers are active in the cosmetics and pharmaceutical sectors at a validated 10,000 EUR per mission price point. Over 500,000 EUR in funding has been secured to date, including equity investment from Climate KIC B.V. and grants from the European Commission (Women TechEU) and Google (Social Tides Grow AI). The platform has reached TRL 6 and is published on the European Commission Horizon Results Platform (ID58919; ID99021). 

Recycllux Malta, incorporated December 2025, is positioned to advance the platform's EO capabilities within ESA's PECS framework, with specific development priorities in detection model accuracy, integration of additional Copernicus data streams and multi-basin transferability starting with the Mediterranean across pan european coastal seas. 

Recycllux operates with a team of ten across eight countries, with 60% women in leadership, and is officially included in the EU Mission "Restore Our Ocean and Waters" Charter.
